criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the ten numbered decisions and the main command-step requirements. The comp-range rules, role-shape restriction, dedupe re-keying, and close-out requirements are all encoded correctly. I found only a minor drift risk in Step 2’s extra `notion-search` option, but no direct contradiction to a numbered decision.

The artifact includes the full Step 0–6 orchestration, schema notes, failure modes, confidence gap section, and the required presentation template. It covers the supplied rulings end-to-end; the only weakness is that one dedupe branch is described a bit more loosely than the command spec.

It follows the project-skill placement convention, avoids the `alex:` prefix, and preserves the required Notion/HITL structure. The markdown is organized conventionally for a skill file. Minor nit: the dedupe section introduces an extra path not named in the orchestration spec.

The skill is lean for its scope and avoids obvious anti-patterns like duplicate state or speculative platforming. I did not see resurrected tombstoned tools or needless ceremony. The extra `notion-search` fallback is the main slight looseness.

There is good failure-mode coverage and an explicit confidence/gap section, but the file also makes a live-verification claim (`re-verified live`) that is not evidenced inside the artifact. That is honest-enough for a note, but still an overclaim for a build artifact and merits a pass-line score.

defects.quote: or notion-search scoped to the Roles data source by the natural key / title company; notion-fetch to confirm.
defects.description: This adds an alternate dedupe path that is not in the supplied orchestration spec, which specifically calls for one bulk SQL read of Content Hash plus the title|company fallback re-key flow. Allowing `notion-search` here weakens the required quota-disciplined dedupe behavior and could reintroduce extra queries.

defects.quote: all endpoints re-verified live that day.
defects.description: The file states live re-verification as fact without any supporting citation or provenance in the artifact itself. That is an overconfident verification claim for a skill doc and hurts auditability.
